newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LATE CANTONA GOAL KEEPS UNITED TOP OF PREMIER LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LATE CANTONA GOAL KEEPS UNITED TOP OF PREMIER LEAGUE.

text.p: An 80th minute strike by Frenchman Eric Cantona gave champions Manchester United a hard-fought 2-1 win over Southampton on Saturday and kept them top of the premier league.
Cantona slid in at the far post to meet a deep cross from Welsh winger Ryan Giggs just as the match appeared to be heading for a draw.
The result avenges two embarrasing defeats suffered by United at Southampton in 1996.
At the end of last season United lost 3-1 at the Dell. They blamed their poor performance on their grey shirts, claiming they made it difficult for their players to see each other.
Then, earlier this season, United crashed 6-3 at Southampton during a dismal run in which they were also routed 5-0 by Newcastle and beaten at home by Fenerbahce, Chelsea and Juventus.

On Saturday Southampton threatened to frustrate United again when they took the lead through Norway's Egil Ostenstad. He jinked past Danish goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel with a neat dummy after 11 minutes to score his 10th goal of the season and his fourth against United following his hat-trick in the epic October clash.

England defender Gary Pallister connected with a Cantona corner to pull United level eight minutes later and, although they failed to dominate the match against a spirited Saints side, Cantona's goal gave them three points.

Liverpool stayed in touch with United by winning 1-0 thanks to a 75th minute strike from Stan Collymore against a Derby side who played virually all of the second half with 10 men after striker Darryl Powell was sent off for a wreckless challenge on Bjorntore Kvarme.
The Merseysiders move into second spot, a point behind United.
Third-placed Arsenal drew 0-0 at Leeds while Wimbledon were held 1-1 at home by bottom side Middlesbrough, for whom Brazilian Emerson missed a penalty.
Wimbledon went ahead through a Neil Cox own goal after 22 minutes but Robbie Mustoe equalised with 15 minutes to play to give Middlesbrough a vital away point in their battle against relegation.
There was also an own goal at White Hart Lane where Chelsea maintained their remarkable run of success against Tottenham with a 2-1 win.

Spurs' England defender Sol Campbell put through his own net after just 50 seconds and Chelsea, without Gianluca Vialli who started on the substitutes' bench despite scoring twice in the 4-2 win over Liverpool last weekend, dominated the clash.
They increased their lead through Vialli's compatriot Roberto Di Matteo. He scored with a stunning 30-metre drive after 53 minutes before Spurs scored a late consolation goal.
Chelsea have lost to their north London rivals just once in their 17 clashes in the 1990s.
Fourth-placed Newcastle entertain Leicester on Sunday.
